question: How does washing your hands thoroughly break the chain of infection?

options.A: It removes the susceptible host entirely
options.B: It eliminates the initial reservoir
options.C: It stops the mode of transmission
options.D: It destroys the infectious agent completely

explanation: Hand hygiene removes germs from your hands, preventing them from traveling from one patient or surface to another. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which part of the nervous system lets you consciously control your skeletal muscles to walk or write?

options.A: Sympathetic nervous system
options.B: Somatic nervous system
options.C: Autonomic nervous system
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: The somatic system handles voluntary movements—the things you decide to do on purpose. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h5)

question: During a serum sickness reaction, where do the troublesome immune complexes usually get trapped?

options.A: Directly on brain cell surfaces
options.B: In small blood vessels and tissues
options.C: Inside large heart valves
options.D: Within the hard bone matrix

explanation: These complexes love to settle down in the tiny filtering blood vessels of places like your joints and skin, causing irritation. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h2)

question: According to Maslow, what must be met before anyone can focus on higher-level needs like self-esteem?

options.A: Peer recognition and leadership roles
options.B: Basic physiological and safety needs
options.C: Advanced professional certifications
options.D: Long-term retirement investment goals

explanation: Think of it like building a house: you need a solid foundation of food, water, and safety before you can worry about chasing big personal goals. [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which part of the teenage brain develops early and drives strong emotions and the search for excitement?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The occipital lobe
options.C: The prefrontal cortex
options.D: The limbic system

explanation: You got this! The limbic system matures early in adolescence, making emotions intense and driving reward-seeking before the brain's rational control center is fully grown. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h1)

question: What happens when a healthcare facility fails to maintain proper family planning records?

options.A: The cost of medical supplies decreases significantly
options.B: Staff members spend less time documenting overall
options.C: Continuity of care breaks down between different shifts and staff
options.D: Clients automatically stop experiencing contraceptive side effects

explanation: Without documented notes, subsequent nurses cannot know what methods were tried, what side effects occurred, or what counsel was given. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h1)

question: What happens in the brain when a nurse experiences an excessively high mental workload?

options.A: Working memory limits are reached and mental shortcuts take over
options.B: Sensory perception shuts down completely for thirty minutes
options.C: The brain instantly doubles its capacity to remember details
options.D: Long-term memory is permanently erased from the mind

explanation: We've all been there! When the brain gets overloaded with too many tasks at once, it relies on quick mental shortcuts, which can unfortunately lead to missed details. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why do labs test for indicator organisms instead of hunting for every single waterborne germ?

options.A: Indicator organisms are much easier and cheaper to detect than all individual pathogens
options.B: Pathogens cannot survive long enough in water samples to be detected in a laboratory
options.C: Indicator organisms completely destroy all other harmful germs present in the water
options.D: Pathogens do not cause waterborne illnesses when consumed in small amounts

explanation: Exactly right! Testing for every rare virus and parasite is tough and expensive. Checking for reliable indicators like E. coli saves time and resources while keeping us safe. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common duty for nurses in a multi-sectorial disaster team?

options.A: Negotiating international trade agreements for relief goods
options.B: Directing military troop movements in the field zone
options.C: Issuing building permits for temporary shelters
options.D: Triaging mass casualties and managing field clinics

explanation: Nurses use their clinical training to sort injured patients and run emergency treatment stations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which of these actions is a serious breach of patient confidentiality?

options.A: Asking a mother for her child's immunization history
options.B: Discussing a patient's HIV status with neighbors at the market
options.C: Reporting anonymous malaria totals to the regional health office
options.D: Storing locked physical clinic registers in the facility record room

explanation: Never share private health details outside the clinic! Gossip destroys patient trust and violates professional ethics. What happens in the clinic stays in the clinic. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is a major cause of cold-loving bacteria contaminating commercial milk?

options.A: Direct sunlight exposure during the transport phase
options.B: High levels of lactose found within the raw liquid
options.C: Improperly cleaned milking equipment and storage tanks
options.D: Natural vitamins added right after the milking process

explanation: Great thinking! When milking gear isn't washed properly, hidden films of bacteria build up and easily slip into the milk, even when it's kept cold. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why do clinical meal plans usually still allow tiny amounts of natural sodium?

options.A: Natural sodium has no effect on human blood pressure
options.B: Basic physiological functions still require small amounts of sodium
options.C: Patients will otherwise refuse to eat any hospital meals
options.D: It helps preserve food for longer periods without refrigeration

explanation: Spot on! Our bodies actually need a little bit of sodium to keep our cells working right, so zero sodium is rarely the goal. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h1)

question: What do the letters SWOT stand for in healthcare management planning?

options.A: Safety, Wellness, Operations, Treatment
options.B: Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats
options.C: Staff, Workflows, Organization, Timing
options.D: Supervision, Wages, Output, Tasks

explanation: SWOT analysis evaluates internal strengths and weaknesses, and external opportunities and threats. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of a nurse's everyday clinical responsibilities?

options.A: Educating the community on the importance of immunization
options.B: Synthesizing laboratory antibodies in a research facility
options.C: Monitoring patients for adverse reactions after vaccination
options.D: Recognizing early clinical signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Growing and building antibodies in a lab is work for researchers and scientists. Nurses focus on patient care, safety, and community health education! [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h9)

question: A family just experienced the peaceful death of a loved one in the hospital. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Advise the family to suppress their tears and stay strong
options.B: Provide a quiet space and time for the family to spend with the body
options.C: Begin discussing hospital billing charges right away
options.D: Ask the family to leave the room immediately so staff can clean

explanation: Allowing family undisturbed time to say a final goodbye is a vital, compassionate part of post-mortem care. You finished this set like a pro! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h8)

question: A patient walks out of a dark cinema into the bright afternoon sun and squints before seeing clearly. What is this quick adjustment called?

options.A: Pupillary constriction
options.B: Dark adaptation
options.C: Light adaptation
options.D: Corneal refraction

explanation: This is light adaptation—your eyes quickly recalibrate when stepping from darkness into bright sunlight. You're smashing it! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why is there usually a noticeable difference between 'perfect use' and 'typical use' success rates for barrier methods?

options.A: People sometimes make mistakes or forget to use them consistently
options.B: Hormonal changes in the user alter how the physical device functions
options.C: The materials degrade instantly the moment the package is opened
options.D: Manufacturers intentionally print lower numbers to avoid lawsuits

explanation: Exactly! Humans aren't robots. Real-life inconsistencies and minor user errors are why typical use rates differ from lab perfection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h4)

question: Why does the herbal supplement St. John's wort often cause prescription drugs to fail?

options.A: It coats the stomach lining and stops all oral tablets from dissolving
options.B: It mimics the chemical structure of insulin and lowers blood sugar
options.C: It induces liver enzymes, causing other drugs to break down too fast
options.D: It binds tightly to vitamin K in the gut and prevents blood clotting

explanation: St. John's wort puts the liver into overdrive! It makes the liver clear out other companion medicines so fast that they leave the body before they even have a chance to work. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h4)

question: What does a psychologically safe nursing classroom help students do?

options.A: Ignore hospital safety guidelines during patient care
options.B: Pass all nursing board examinations without studying
options.C: Skip difficult clinical shifts without facing any penalties
options.D: Admit what they do not know without fear of harsh judgment

explanation: When you feel safe, you can freely speak up about mistakes or confusion without being judged. That openness is key to keeping patients safe in the clinic! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h3)

question: What is the main goal of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in treating disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: To immediately repair severed nerve axons overnight
options.B: To reduce relapse frequency and slow long-term disability
options.C: To completely cure the underlying autoimmune response
options.D: To lower elevated blood pressure caused by stress

explanation: While they don't offer an instant cure, DMTs help calm the immune system over time, preventing future attacks and keeping the patient independent longer. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: What distinct, tough patch does the diphtheria bacterium form in the throat?

options.A: A tough gray pseudomembrane
options.B: A widespread fatty liver
options.C: A fluid-filled skin blister
options.D: A hard calcified granuloma

explanation: Diphtheria creates a stubborn gray coating (pseudomembrane) in the airway made of dead cells, bacteria, and clotting proteins that can block breathing. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does community stigma negatively affect disease surveillance data?

options.A: It speeds up the transmission of weekly health reports to the capital.
options.B: It causes people to hide sick family members and avoid visiting clinics.
options.C: It automatically increases the national budget allocation for health.
options.D: It forces laboratories to buy more expensive testing equipment.

explanation: When people are scared of being judged or isolated, they hide their illnesses at home, leading to missing cases and inaccurate health stats. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h8)

question: Why does clearing stagnant water around your compound help stop malaria?

options.A: It destroys the breeding sites where mosquitoes lay their eggs
options.B: It cools down the ambient temperature to kill flying insects
options.C: It prevents houseflies from walking on contaminated garbage
options.D: It poisons adult rats before they can enter the kitchen

explanation: Spot on! Mosquitoes need standing water to lay their eggs and grow. No stagnant water means fewer mosquitoes! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h5)

question: How do effective unit managers keep patients safe during tough staff and resource shortages?

options.A: By charging patients exorbitant fees for basic cotton wool
options.B: By pretending that the shortages do not exist at all
options.C: By turning away every single patient who walks through the door
options.D: By using creative resourcefulness and strong advocacy skills

explanation: Brilliant! Even when resources are tight, resourceful managers find safe workarounds and fight hard for what their ward needs. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)

question: What makes providing home health care different from working in a hospital ward?

options.A: There are always doctors present during every shift
options.B: Patients have no say in their daily routines
options.C: Medical equipment is never required in the home
options.D: The nurse operates inside the patient's private residence

explanation: You're stepping into the patient's personal space! Unlike controlled hospital wards, home care means dealing with everyday home environments and variables. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main difference between active failures and latent conditions?

options.A: Active failures are committed by frontline workers, while latent conditions are hidden system flaws
options.B: Active failures only happen at night, while latent conditions occur during daytime shifts
options.C: Active failures are hidden system flaws, while latent conditions are direct staff mistakes
options.D: Active failures cause minor paperwork delays, while latent conditions always cause patient death

explanation: Think of active failures as slip-ups made right at the bedside, while latent conditions are hidden design or organizational traps waiting quietly in the background. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which cells turn into antibody-producing factories during humoral immunity?

options.A: Thymocytes
options.B: Plasma cells
options.C: Platelets
options.D: Erythrocytes

explanation: When B-cells get activated, they transform into plasma cells whose full-time job is pumping out antibodies. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is checking blood sugar one of the first things to do when caring for an unresponsive patient?

options.A: Hypoglycemia is a metabolic cause of altered consciousness that can be quickly reversed
options.B: Glucose checks replace the need for a neurological exam
options.C: High blood sugar directly damages the brainstem within minutes
options.D: Diabetes mellitus is the primary cause of all neurological trauma

explanation: Spot on! Low blood sugar starves the brain of energy, causing unconsciousness that can fix itself almost instantly once glucose is given. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is an important nursing task when dealing with different healthcare levels?

options.A: Setting the financial prices for private hospital medications
options.B: Guiding patients smoothly through appropriate referral pathways
options.C: Managing government tax allocations for public health centers
options.D: Issuing official operating licenses to traditional birth attendants

explanation: You're a star! Nurses use their knowledge of facility tiers to make sure patients get sent to the exact right place for their condition. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h6)

question: A young patient is scared that birth control pills cause permanent infertility because of community rumors. What is your best response?

options.A: Confirm her fears and suggest she never use any form of modern medicine
options.B: Provide calm, factual education explaining that fertility returns after stopping
options.C: Refuse to prescribe any medication until she agrees to stop asking questions
options.D: Scold the patient for listening to uneducated members of the community

explanation: You're a health educator! Always meet patient fears with patience and facts, reassuring them that fertility bounces back once they stop taking the pills. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h8)

question: Why do nurses prefer using a large-bore cannula (like an 18-gauge) for blood transfusions?

options.A: It prevents the physical damage and destruction of red blood cells
options.B: It prevents the IV site from swelling or leaking into the tissues
options.C: It allows the nurse to infuse multiple medications at the same time
options.D: It reduces the need to check vital signs during the first fifteen minutes

explanation: Think of it like a wide pipe versus a tiny straw—narrow needles can squeeze and break fragile red blood cells, causing damage. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h4)

question: Which stage of wastewater treatment relies mainly on physical screening and letting solids settle?

options.A: Primary treatment
options.B: Secondary treatment
options.C: Quaternary treatment
options.D: Tertiary treatment

explanation: Primary treatment is the first physical cleanup step. It uses large screens and settling tanks to catch big debris and let heavy particles drop out of the water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary digestive function of the oral cavity?

options.A: Absorption of complex carbohydrates into the bloodstream
options.B: Production of powerful hydrochloric acid to sterilize food
options.C: Complete enzymatic breakdown and absorption of proteins
options.D: Mechanical breakdown of food and mixing it with saliva

explanation: The mouth starts digestion by chewing food into smaller pieces and mixing it with saliva to create an easy-to-swallow bolus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h1)

question: In global polio campaigns, what does the abbreviation 'AFP' stand for?

options.A: Asymmetrical Facial Palsy
options.B: Active Fever Protocol
options.C: Advanced Functional Pathology
options.D: Acute Flaccid Paralysis

explanation: You're doing great! AFP stands for acute flaccid paralysis—the key sign health workers watch out for to catch hidden polio cases early. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h6)

question: What happens when food moves way too quickly through a person's colon?

options.A: Ulceration
options.B: Appendicitis
options.C: Diarrhea
options.D: Constipation

explanation: If food rushes through the colon, there's no time to absorb water, leading to loose, watery stools. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does the high humidity inside a steam tent help a patient with a heavy cough?

options.A: It dilates the tiny air sacs in the lower lungs
options.B: It kills bacterial infections in the upper airway
options.C: It numbs the throat nerves to stop the cough reflex
options.D: It liquefies thick mucus so it is easier to clear

explanation: Spot on! Moisture acts like magic on sticky mucus, thinning it out so the patient can cough it up easily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is it important to use a mix of different data collection tools during a community diagnosis?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by international pharmaceutical companies
options.B: It reduces the amount of time needed to write the final report
options.C: It helps verify findings and provides a more complete picture of health needs
options.D: It ensures that every single resident is interviewed personally

explanation: Combining surveys, interviews, and observations allows nurses to cross-verify data and understand both numbers and human experiences. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: If a fuel tanker explodes in a busy local market, which teams need to rush to the scene right away?

options.A: Fire Service, Police Force, and Emergency Healthcare Providers
options.B: Immigration Service, Tax Board, and Agricultural Extension Workers
options.C: Postal Service, Sports Commission, and Public Library
options.D: Customs Service, Judiciary, and Primary Education Board

explanation: You nailed it! A major fire needs firefighters to put it out, police to manage the crowd and secure the area, and health workers to treat burns and injuries. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h3)

question: What happens when a healthcare market reaches 'equilibrium'?

options.A: Healthcare services become completely free of charge
options.B: The supply of doctors far exceeds patient demand
options.C: Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
options.D: Hospital bed shortages disappear permanently everywhere

explanation: Perfect! Equilibrium just means a sweet balance: the amount of care people want matches what the health system is able to give. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is it a bad idea to use young family members as language interpreters?

options.A: Hospital policies fine families for using child translators
options.B: It can lead to translation errors and breach patient privacy
options.C: Children refuse to speak during home health visits
options.D: Children are always better at medical terminology than adults

explanation: Medical terms are tough to translate, and it puts an unfair emotional burden on a child to handle sensitive health matters for their relative. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the standard core rights of medication administration?

options.A: Right dose
options.B: Right manufacturer
options.C: Right time
options.D: Right patient

explanation: The core medication rights focus on the patient, drug, dose, route, time, and documentation, rather than the specific company that manufactured the product. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which problem is most likely to happen if someone has a severe lack of dietary fat?

options.A: Dangerous spikes in blood sugar
options.B: Trouble absorbing vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.C: An enlarged thyroid gland
options.D: Too much good cholesterol in the blood

explanation: Remember, fat-soluble vitamins need dietary fat to get absorbed! Without enough fat, deficiency symptoms start to show up. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h4)

question: What are the three core parts of the famous epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Source, vector, and cure
options.B: Bacteria, virus, and parasite
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Infection, symptom, and recovery

explanation: Never forget the classic trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (the surroundings). You've got this memorized now! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h6)

question: Why is malaria prevention especially critical for individuals living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Anti-malarial medications cure the underlying genetic mutation permanently
options.B: Malaria infection triggers severe red blood cell sickling and life-threatening crises
options.C: Malaria parasites feed directly on normal adult haemoglobin A exclusively
options.D: Fever from malaria permanently stops the bone marrow from making blood

explanation: Fever, inflammation, and red blood cell destruction caused by malaria are powerful triggers that induce widespread vessel blockage in sickle cell patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which two organs get a much-needed rest when you lower dietary fat?

options.A: Kidneys and urinary bladder
options.B: Pancreas and gallbladder
options.C: Spleen and large intestine
options.D: Thyroid and parathyroid glands

explanation: Great thinking! The pancreas and gallbladder work hard to break down fats, so cutting back gives them time to rest and heal. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h2)

question: A patient inhales respiratory droplets from a coughing roommate. What link in the chain does the respiratory tract represent for this new patient?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Mode of transmission
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: The respiratory tract is the physical pathway through which the pathogen enters the body of the susceptible host. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h2)

question: Why is writing 'patient seems uncooperative' discouraged in nursing notes?

options.A: It takes too much time to write out compared to numbers
options.B: It prevents doctors from prescribing pain medication
options.C: It is subjective and reflects personal bias rather than facts
options.D: It violates hospital billing guidelines and insurance rules

explanation: Labels like 'uncooperative' are just opinions. Instead, write the clear facts of what happened, like 'patient refused morning vital signs.' [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h4)

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer comes in with a swollen right leg and dull flank pain. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Metastatic spread of cancer cells to the bones of the foot
options.B: Tumor compression of pelvic veins and the ureter
options.C: Development of deep vein thrombosis from excessive physical activity
options.D: Severe systemic dehydration caused by heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Makes sense when you picture it: a growing tumor in the pelvis can press against nearby blood vessels (causing leg swelling) and block the tubes leading from the kidneys, known as the ureters (causing flank pain). [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the mandatory retirement age for public servants in the Nigerian civil service?

options.A: 60 years
options.B: 70 years
options.C: 50 years
options.D: 65 years

explanation: In the Nigerian civil service, the rule is to retire at 60 years of age or after 35 years of active service—whichever comes first! [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h8)

question: A student wants to study post-operative pain across fifty hospitals nationwide in just two weeks with zero funding. What is the major flaw here?

options.A: Patients do not experience pain after surgery
options.B: The topic is completely unrelated to nursing care
options.C: Hospital staff never want to improve pain management
options.D: The study lacks practical feasibility due to time and budget limits

explanation: We would all love to save the world in two weeks for free, but it's simply not realistic! Always make sure your study matches your actual time and pockets. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h6)

question: A patient loves the extra sympathy and gets excused from chores because of physical complaints that doctors can't find a medical cause for. What is this called?

options.A: Primary gain
options.B: Secondary gain
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Neuroplasticity

explanation: Spot on! Secondary gain refers to the external perks—like extra care, sympathy, or getting out of house chores—that come along with playing the sick role. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which imaging tool uses high-frequency sound waves instead of radiation?

options.A: PET scan
options.B: X-ray
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: CT scan

explanation: Ultrasound relies on sound waves bouncing off internal organs to form a picture, avoiding the radiation used in X-rays and CT scans. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: What simple question did Bernardino Ramazzini say doctors must always ask their patients?

options.A: What is your occupation?
options.B: How many hours do you sleep?
options.C: Where do you buy your food?
options.D: What is your family medical history?

explanation: Ramazzini realized that a patient's job is often the biggest clue to what is making them sick. Always remember to check your patient's work background! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h3)

question: What should a nursing team do during the 'Study' phase of a PDSA cycle?

options.A: Purchase new equipment for every unit in the entire hospital
options.B: Compare the actual results to their original predictions and analyze what happened
options.C: Write a formal disciplinary warning for staff who failed to follow instructions
options.D: Design a brand new aim statement from scratch

explanation: Spot on! The Study phase is all about looking at your data and figuring out why the test turned out the way it did. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the main goal of descriptive statistics in a study?

options.A: Summarize the basic features and scores of the sample data
options.B: Replace the need for taking patient medical histories
options.C: Prove that a new drug cures a disease in all humans
options.D: Determine the financial cost of running a hospital ward

explanation: Descriptive statistics give you a quick, clear snapshot of what your sample looks like using simple summaries like averages and percentages. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h4)

question: Your patient cannot lift their hips off the bed to get a bedpan underneath. What is the safest way to help them?

options.A: Raise the head of the bed to the high Fowler position before sliding the pan downward
options.B: Forcefully slide the standard bedpan underneath the patient using maximum pulling force
options.C: Leave the patient without a bedpan until a doctor writes a specific order to lift them
options.D: Roll the patient onto their side, place the bedpan against the buttocks, and roll them back

explanation: Never force equipment under a patient! Rolling them gently onto a properly placed pan protects their delicate skin from friction and painful shearing forces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h2)

question: What does the tech phrase 'garbage in, garbage out' mean for nursing documentation?

options.A: All hospital trash must be sorted before entering the electronic system
options.B: Inaccurate data entry leads to unreliable clinical reports and decisions
options.C: Patient records must be printed and thrown away every evening
options.D: Computers automatically delete any notes typed by junior nurses

explanation: It makes total sense: if sloppy or incorrect data goes into the computer, the resulting clinical alerts and reports will also be completely wrong. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why does societal stigma directly harm the success of a sheltered workshop?

options.A: It causes the workshop building to physically collapse
options.B: It prevents nurses from administering oral medications
options.C: The public may refuse to buy products made by the clients
options.D: It forces workers to labor for twenty-four hours a day

explanation: Negative public attitudes make it hard to sell products, which hurts the financial survival of the workshop. You've got this! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h5)

question: How does a community health nurse use epidemiological thinking during a clinic shift?

options.A: By focusing strictly on the medical chart of the person in front of them
options.B: By ordering expensive scans for every patient with a headache
options.C: By looking for patterns and causes of illness in the local community
options.D: By diagnosing complex genetic disorders without lab tests

explanation: Exactly! Community health nurses connect the dots between individual illnesses and broader local trends to help everyone stay healthy. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: Why is the smoke that comes off tissues during laser or electrocautery surgery considered a health hazard?

options.B: It instantly blinds anyone not wearing dark glasses

question: How can you use nursing informatics to support evidence-based practice right at your patient's bedside?

question: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of a good healthcare plan?

question: Which type of precautions must you use for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

question: How is it possible for a patient to be overweight and still suffer from malnutrition?

question: Why do we prefer single-dose medication vials over multi-dose vials in clinical practice?

question: How does a researcher's philosophical viewpoint shape a qualitative study?

question: What is the main goal of using a chest drain to remove air or fluid from the chest cavity?

question: What does data triangulation mean in community health assessment?

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling vector-borne diseases like malaria in a community?

options.C: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy adult

question: What is the main job of the support nurse when family members are allowed in the room during an active emergency resuscitation?

question: What is the main difference between quarantine and isolation?

question: Why is growing different types of crops (crop diversity) on small farms good for community nutrition?

question: Why is a delicate balance of hemostasis important for a patient?

question: Why are nurses considered central to safe waste management in a hospital?

question: What is the general outlook for a patient who gets steady medical and psychological care for OCD?

question: Which family clue in a patient's medical history raises her risk for endometriosis?

question: Why must you NEVER put anything in a patient's mouth while they are having a generalized seizure?

question: Why are women biologically more at risk of getting STIs than men?

question: Why must you let the alcohol skin cleanser dry completely before giving an intradermal injection?

question: Which type of artificial fat, made by industrial processing, is best avoided entirely?

question: Which of these is NOT a standard rule when picking essential medicines?

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause of a workplace accident?

question: What is the main purpose of a health screening test?

question: What is a common dietary consequence for workers holding multiple exhausting jobs?

options.D: It eliminates all forms of human bias automatically

explanation: No need to wait years! Cross-sectional studies save precious time and money because everything happens in one go. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the right nursing action when you spot rigid, overlapping skull bones on a newborn?

options.A: Document the finding and monitor without forcing the bones apart
options.B: Apply warm compresses to soften the cranial sutures
options.C: Gently massage the bones back into a normal round shape
options.D: Wrap the head tightly with a bandage to keep bones in place

explanation: Brilliant! Never try to push or massage overlapping bones back into place—that can cause more injury. Just document what you see and keep a close eye on the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h5)

question: What is a reservoir in the chain of infection?

options.A: The method used by a microbe to travel to a new host
options.B: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.C: The specific entry point through broken skin
options.D: A person who has complete immunity against disease

explanation: A reservoir acts as the home base where germs live, grow, and reproduce before moving to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric rehabilitation?

options.A: Keeping patients sedated in a quiet environment
options.B: Preventing family members from visiting the ward
options.C: Helping patients return to independent community living
options.D: Testing new high-dose antipsychotic drugs

explanation: Psychiatric rehab is all about helping individuals get back to living, working, and learning in their communities with confidence and independence! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: When are outbreaks of water-borne diseases like cholera most common in Nigeria?

options.A: In the middle of the hot dry summer months
options.B: During the rainy season when floods overwhelm sanitation
options.C: Right after major harvesting periods end
options.D: During the dry harmattan season when dust increases

explanation: Heavy rains wash surface waste into shallow wells and boreholes, spreading contamination rapidly during the rainy season. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is treating the root cause the most important step when caring for a patient with DIC?

options.A: It stops the continuous, abnormal activation of the clotting cascade.
options.B: It immediately replaces all lost red blood cells and platelets.
options.C: It reverses the inherited genetic mutation causing the disease.
options.D: It prevents the patient from experiencing allergic reactions to plasma.

explanation: DIC is triggered by an underlying problem like an infection or severe injury. Until you fix that main trigger, the body will just keep overusing its clotting resources! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h7)

question: A patient with a fever is breathing fast and sweating. What kind of fluid loss is happening here?

options.A: Measurable fluid output
options.B: Third-space fluid shift
options.C: Insensible fluid loss
options.D: Gastrointestinal loss

explanation: Exactly! It's called 'insensible' because we can't easily measure it with a jug or a catheter—it just silently evaporates away through breath and skin. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why is getting enough folate so crucial for women of reproductive age?

options.A: It maintains bone density in the lower spine
options.B: It stops heavy bleeding during the menstrual cycle
options.C: It directly increases daily red blood cell counts
options.D: It prevents neural tube defects in early pregnancy

explanation: Exactly right! Folate helps cells divide rapidly and protects the baby's developing spine and brain during the very early weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand local Nigerian food habits?

options.A: It allows the nurse to restrict patient access to local markets
options.B: It serves as the best foundation for practical dietary recommendations
options.C: It helps the nurse completely replace traditional meals with foreign diets
options.D: It is only useful for hospital kitchen staff preparation

explanation: Great nursing care meets patients where they are! Working with familiar cultural foods ensures your nutrition advice is realistic, affordable, and actually gets used at home. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h1)

question: At what age does a healthy baby usually double their birth weight?

options.A: At 9 months of age
options.B: At 12 months of age
options.C: At 2 months of age
options.D: At 5 months of age

explanation: Great job! A baby typically doubles their birth weight around 5 months and triples it by their first birthday. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which behavioral change is a classic warning sign of potential substance abuse?

options.A: Neglecting work or school responsibilities
options.B: Consistent weight gain and healthy skin tone
options.C: An increased interest in family activities
options.D: Sudden improvement in daily sleep routines

explanation: Correct! When substances take center stage in someone's life, important commitments like classes, work, and family duties usually start slipping away. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h5)

question: A patient suddenly develops severe shortness of breath and chest pain after a long plane ride. Which condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Left ventricular failure

explanation: Immobility during a long trip can lead to blood clots in the legs that break off and travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why do pure scare tactics usually fail in teenage drug education programs?

options.A: Adolescents lack the physical ability to listen to spoken English instructions
options.B: Teens may find the exaggerated warnings do not match their real-world observations
options.C: Young people prefer reading detailed legal textbooks over listening to talks
options.D: Scare tactics automatically cure physical tolerance within twenty-four hours

explanation: When young people see friends using substances without immediate disaster, over-the-top scare stories lose all credibility. Honest, factual education works best! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h3)

question: In simple terms, what does 'demand' mean when we talk about health services?

options.A: The total amount of care that patients want and can use
options.B: The cost of buying medical equipment from abroad
options.C: The total number of doctors in a government hospital
options.D: The maximum number of beds a health center can hold

explanation: You've got this! Demand simply means the healthcare services people need and are able to access. Think of it as the care patients are asking for and using. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h1)

question: What standard framework guides disease reporting forms in Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: Standard Operating Procedures for Pharmacy Inventory
options.B: National Curriculum for Basic Nursing Education
options.C: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR)
options.D: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

explanation: IDSR is the golden framework we use across Nigerian facilities to keep our disease tracking organized and consistent. You'll see this a lot in practice! [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)
